news.title: Peak surcharges hit oversize packages now and home deliveries from Oct 24 to 26
news.sum: Peak fees on additional handling, large and over-max packages have billed since Sep 26 to 28 at OnTrac, UPS and FedEx. Per-package fees start next: OnTrac $1.00 on Oct 24, UPS and Amazon Shipping $0.50 on Oct 25, FedEx $0.50 on Oct 26. UPS and Amazon rise to $0.75 from Nov 22 to Dec 26, FedEx to $0.80 from Nov 23 to Dec 27. Amazon charges per package with no separate residential surcharge, and its handling fees wait until Oct 25.
news.plain: Standard peak fees add $0.50 to $1.00 to residential ground packages from late October, rising to $0.75 to $0.80 at UPS, FedEx and Amazon in the late-November to December peak weeks. UPS and FedEx shippers above 20,000 residential packages a week pay higher tiered charges.

news.title: FAA drone delivery rule (Part 108) still unpublished
news.sum: The FAA sent its Part 108 beyond-visual-line-of-sight final rule to White House review on July 10, 2026, after missing a Feb. 1 executive-order deadline. As of Oct. 9 the rule had not been published. Until it takes effect, routine BVLOS delivery still needs waivers or Part 135 certificates.
news.plain: Wider drone delivery beyond today's waiver-based sites depends on when the rule is published.
news.tie: Zipline has said the uncertainty is holding back investment.

news.title: UPS plans 100,000+ seasonal hires and adds a $10.70 PIN-protected delivery option
news.sum: UPS said it is hiring more than 100,000 seasonal workers and expects more than 4 billion RFID-enabled packages by the end of 2026. It also launched Protected Delivery, which requires the recipient to give the driver a PIN before release. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported the option costs $10.70 per package and that UPS expects U.S. volume to rise about 24% from the third quarter to the fourth.
news.plain: Optional paid service: Protected Delivery adds $10.70 per package. No change to base rates.
news.tie: FedEx launched a $20 QR-code Authenticated Delivery option on Oct 2.

news.title: Logistics Managers' Index hits 70.2 as transportation prices climb
news.sum: The September 2026 Logistics Managers' Index was 70.2. Transportation Prices were 92.7, Transportation Capacity 34.4 and Transportation Utilization 66.1; Inventory Costs were 79.9 and Warehousing Prices 73.5.
news.plain: Shows tight transportation capacity and steep price increases heading into peak. It measures logistics broadly, not parcel alone.

news.title: Ground fuel surcharges ease for the first time in four weeks
news.sum: UPS ground fuel fell to 29.75% and FedEx to 29.25% for the week of Oct 5, each down 0.50 points after three straight increases. OnTrac eased to 27.00% from 27.50%, and its own page already lists 26.50% for the week of Oct 12.
news.plain: Ground fuel on a $12 package is about 6 cents lower than last week. Rates remain near their 2026 high.

srcs.src: OnTrac surcharges page (spotted by Parcel Pigeon)

news.title: USPS holiday prices take effect on four package products
news.sum: USPS raised prices on Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail and Ground Advantage (retail and commercial) and Parcel Select (commercial) from Oct 4 through Jan 16; trade press puts the average near 6%. Commercial Ground Advantage under 3 lb rises $0.40 in Zones 1–4 and $0.55 in Zones 5–9.
news.plain: USPS builds the increase into the label price rather than a separate fee. On zoned products the farther zones rise more; Parcel Select rises by the same amount in every zone.

news.title: UPS has not yet announced 2027 rates
news.sum: UPS hasn't announced its 2027 GRI. In recent years it has followed FedEx by two to three weeks and matched the 5.9% headline.
news.plain: UPS 2027 list prices are not yet published. FedEx and DHL have each set a 5.9% average.

news.title: Report: Amazon's backup plan would take its own delivery to 95% of U.S. ZIP codes by 2029
news.sum: Business Insider reported on 'Project Aurelian,' an internal Amazon contingency plan drawn up in case its USPS agreement fell through. It would extend Amazon's own delivery network to about 95% of U.S. ZIP codes (roughly 39,400) and 99.9% of customer demand by 2029, with each ZIP also covered by at least one outside carrier.
news.plain: No current change. Amazon and USPS later agreed to keep about 80% of Amazon's USPS volume; the plan shows how far Amazon has mapped its own coverage.
news.tie: Amazon and USPS reached their new agreement in April 2026, and USPS began a same-day pilot for Amazon in September.

news.title: UPS and FedEx add paid theft and fraud protection, including a $20 QR-code delivery check
news.sum: UPS bundled insurance, theft-reducing label options and checkout fraud screening into Secure Commerce. FedEx added Authenticated Delivery, where the recipient shows a QR code before handover, at $20 on select express services in the U.S. and Canada. Hold at Location and redirects aren't available on those shipments, and they go back to the sender after up to three delivery attempts.
news.plain: Optional paid services. FedEx Authenticated Delivery costs $20 on select express services in the U.S. and Canada.

news.title: FedEx completes $1.4B sale of FedEx Supply Chain to CMA CGM
news.sum: FedEx Supply Chain, its warehousing and distribution unit, now belongs to CMA CGM and folds into CEVA Logistics. CEVA says the deal nearly triples its North American contract logistics business, and CMA CGM becomes a preferred ocean carrier for FedEx under a non-exclusive agreement.
news.plain: No change to FedEx parcel service. FedEx Supply Chain warehousing contracts move to CEVA Logistics.

news.title: NYC coalition maps 14,000+ citations on Amazon-linked delivery vans
news.sum: A labor and community coalition mapped more than 14,000 traffic and parking citations on Amazon-linked delivery vehicles from mid-2021 to mid-2025. It backs a proposed city law, the Delivery Protection Act, that would license last-mile delivery stations and require them to directly employ their core warehouse workers.
news.plain: No current rule change. The coalition backs a proposed city law to license last-mile delivery stations.

news.title: USPS pilots same-day delivery for Amazon with a midday drop
news.sum: Amazon drops a second batch at select post offices between noon and 1 p.m. for delivery by 8 p.m. The pilot was set to start Sep 29 in two small cities, capped at 200 packages a day per site. Columbia, S.C., joins Oct 20 with a 500-package cap.
news.plain: The pilot carries Amazon packages, in two cities now, with Columbia, S.C., added Oct 20.

news.title: Amazon adds LTL labels and regional pricing for bulky orders
news.sum: Starting in October, sellers can buy less-than-truckload labels through Amazon Buy Shipping at Amazon-negotiated rates with late-delivery protection. Regional delivery pricing for heavy and bulky items arrives in early 2027, and Amazon will connect sellers with local carriers for same- or next-day delivery within 100 miles.
news.plain: Amazon sellers can buy LTL labels through Buy Shipping starting in October. Regional pricing for heavy and bulky items starts in early 2027.

news.title: FedEx orders 2,000 Harbinger electric delivery trucks
news.sum: The trucks replace diesel pickup and delivery vehicles one for one in the U.S. and Canada, with all units due by the end of 2027. Harbinger estimates about $20,000 a year in fuel savings per truck. FedEx targets an all-electric pickup and delivery fleet by 2040.
news.plain: No rate change. The trucks replace diesel pickup and delivery vehicles through 2027.

news.title: DoorDash adds Macy's, Anthropologie and VF brands, launches $7.99 courier returns
news.sum: DoorDash added Macy's (350+ stores), Anthropologie (220+ stores) and VF Corp's The North Face, Vans and Timberland (350+ stores) to its marketplace. It also launched Dasher returns: a flat $7.99 per return with no box or label, pickup in as little as 30 minutes, and the item taken back to the store it came from. Returns are live in select cities, with a U.S. rollout expected in November.
news.plain: Store-bound courier returns skip carrier labels and drop-off points, so some e-commerce return volume could move from carrier reverse networks to gig couriers.
news.tie: Follows the Uber Eats courier returns launch in April 2026. DoorDash's 2022 'Return a Package' beta instead took prepaid-label parcels to UPS, FedEx and USPS drop-off points.

news.title: DoorDash unveils delivery drones it designed in-house
news.sum: DoorDash unveiled six-rotor aircraft it designed and built for its DoorDash Air service and plans pilot deliveries with them, while keeping its Wing and Flytrex partnerships. Test flights in Northern California average under five minutes. DoorDash says about 80% of its U.S. restaurant orders fit the aircraft's size and weight limits, before distance and weather.
news.plain: A large gig platform is moving to fly its own aircraft rather than rely only on third-party drone operators.
news.tie: Announced the same day as DoorDash's $7.99 returns service.

news.title: UPS's Happy Returns adds box-free returns for TikTok Shop sellers
news.sum: TikTok Shop added Happy Returns, owned by UPS, for no-box, no-label returns at nearly 10,000 U.S. drop-off points in The UPS Store, Staples and Ulta Beauty locations. The service is included for Fulfilled by TikTok sellers; self-shipping sellers must opt in. Happy Returns consolidates items and ships them to sellers in bulk through UPS.
news.plain: Consolidated returns cut the number of individual return labels and move marketplace return volume into UPS's network.
news.tie: FedEx offers a competing no-box option through FedEx Office and Kohl's; DoorDash and Uber now offer courier returns.

news.title: Adobe forecasts $275.1 billion in U.S. holiday online sales, up 6.7%
news.sum: Adobe Digital Insights forecasts $275.1 billion in U.S. online sales from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026, up 6.7%. Cyber Week is projected at $47.5 billion (+7.4%) and Cyber Monday at $15.1 billion (+6.2%).
news.plain: Points to mid-single-digit growth in holiday e-commerce, the main driver of peak parcel volume.

news.title: DHL Express sets 5.9% average increase for U.S. accounts on Jan 1, 2027
news.sum: DHL Express announced a 5.9% general average price adjustment for U.S. account holders, effective January 1, 2027. A limited number of services and surcharges will also change; DHL did not list them.
news.plain: DHL Express list rates rise an average 5.9% from Jan 1, 2027. Increases vary by service.

news.title: GOFO reports 47-state network, 12,000+ ZIP codes
news.sum: GOFO, a last-mile carrier founded in Los Angeles in 2023, says it operates 300+ hubs and stations covering over 75% of the U.S. population. Its white paper, citing ShipMatrix, puts 2025 U.S. parcel volume at 23.9 billion, with carriers outside UPS, FedEx and USPS handling about 2.5 billion, up roughly 13%.
news.plain: GOFO says it reached its 12,000-ZIP coverage goal; its population coverage, over 75%, is still short of the roughly 82% in that goal. It announced the Cirro E-Commerce acquisition in February.

news.title: Lowe's starts drone delivery pilot with Wing and DoorDash near Charlotte
news.sum: Lowe's began drone delivery from its Matthews, N.C., store through the DoorDash app using Wing drones. More than 100 items are eligible, with payloads of about 2.5 pounds and delivery in as little as 20 minutes.
news.plain: Tests drone delivery for small home-improvement items that would otherwise ship as parcels or go by courier.
news.tie: Wing also flies for Walmart, which is expanding drone delivery to more than 270 stores in 2026.

news.title: Teamsters signal possible UPS strike in 2028
news.sum: Teamsters president Sean O'Brien has said a strike is likely when the UPS contract ends July 31, 2028, and has floated coordinating with West Coast dockworkers, whose contract expires a month earlier, on July 1, 2028.
news.plain: The UPS–Teamsters contract ends July 31, 2028; the West Coast port contract ends July 1, 2028.

news.title: Dollar General and Instacart start no-markup delivery, targeting 20,000 stores
news.sum: Dollar General and Instacart are rolling out no-markup same-day delivery, now at about 7,000 stores, with plans to cover all roughly 20,000 stores in 48 states this fall. Dollar General said delivery added 40 basis points to comparable sales and brought in more than a million new customers. It plans to pilot a delivery subscription before year-end.
news.plain: Extends on-demand delivery into rural ZIP codes that national carriers often serve with residential and delivery-area surcharges.
news.tie: Builds on Dollar General's January 2026 myDG same-day expansion to more than 17,000 stores.

news.title: Veritiv launches compact cold-chain canister aimed at GLP-1 shipments
news.sum: Veritiv launched TempSafe RxShield, a canister of about 240 grams that holds four 10 mL vials at refrigerated temperatures for up to 36 hours, validated to ISTA 7E. Veritiv says it cuts dimensional weight by up to 30%.
news.plain: Smaller insulated packaging lowers the billable dimensional weight of mail-order refrigerated prescriptions.

news.title: Diesel hits a record $6.53 a gallon
news.sum: The national average diesel price reached $6.53 a gallon for the week of Sep 21, up from $5.60 at the end of August and above the previous weekly high of $5.81 set in June 2022, per U.S. Energy Information Administration data.
news.plain: Ground fuel surcharges follow diesel with a short lag; UPS uses the EIA price from the week before. September's rise preceded the late-September fuel peak.

news.title: USPS inspector general: undeliverable "dead mail" packages up 45%
news.sum: A USPS Office of Inspector General report on the Mail Recovery Center found dead mail (packages that can be neither delivered nor returned) rose 45% over a recent 12-month period, and customers filed 5 million missing-package complaints in FY 2025. It makes nine recommendations.
news.plain: More USPS packages are ending up undeliverable and unreturnable.
news.tie: Related to the inspector general's finding that USPS lost $163 million as fulfillment centers refused undeliverable returns.

news.title: FedEx adds per-pound demand fees on U.S. imports, raises export fees
news.sum: FedEx now charges per-pound demand surcharges on imports into the U.S. from Canada ($0.14), Latin America and the Caribbean ($0.12), and Europe and Israel ($0.25). Its export demand fee to Canada, Latin America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand rose from $0.20 to $0.30 a pound. Both run until further notice.
news.plain: New import fees of $0.12 to $0.25 a pound from those regions; imports from Asia rose the same day, to $0.54 to $0.91. Exports to those regions now pay $0.30 a pound. FedEx lists demand surcharges among the charges its fuel surcharge applies to.

news.title: FedEx sets 5.9% average increase for Jan 4, 2027
news.sum: Light Ground weights rise faster than the average (about 6.5% for 1–5 lb, per an analysis by Loop), many surcharges rise more, two paper-document fees start Jan 18, and zones change for select U.S. ZIP code pairs on Feb 1.
news.plain: List rates rise an average 5.9% on Jan 4. A $25 Paper Document Fee and a $5 Paper Air Waybill Fee start Jan 18, and zone classifications change for select U.S. ZIP code pairs Feb 1.

news.title: DoorDash and Uber Eats both expand Costco delivery nationwide
news.sum: Uber Eats expanded Costco delivery to nearly 600 warehouses in 47 states on Sept. 16, up from 17 states under its 2024 agreement. A day later DoorDash announced delivery from all U.S. Costco warehouses (639 stores in 47 states). Both require a Costco membership; DoorDash did not disclose fees or a launch date.
news.plain: Club-store merchandise is now available for same-day gig delivery across most of the U.S., competing with ground parcel for household restocking orders.
news.tie: Costco has used Instacart for nearly a decade.

news.title: Report: Postmaster General has told associates he wants to resign
news.sum: Reuters reported, citing four people familiar with his thinking, that Postmaster General David Steiner, in the job since July 2025, has told associates he is discouraged and wants to step down. USPS said the report has 'absolutely zero validity.' Steiner has told Congress that without new funding USPS may have to cut delivery days and close unprofitable post offices.
news.plain: No change to USPS service or prices.

news.title: Amazon to seek delay of March 2027 FTC antitrust trial
news.sum: Amazon plans to ask about postponing its FTC antitrust trial, now set for March 29, 2027, after a state judge moved California's separate antitrust trial against Amazon from Jan. 19 to March 22. The FTC case covers marketplace practices the agency has tied to sellers' use of Amazon fulfillment.
news.plain: Pushes back any court ruling on Amazon's marketplace and fulfillment practices.

news.title: OnTrac launches Dynamic Savings and names a new CTO
news.sum: OnTrac's Dynamic Savings, built with Onrout, offers promotional rates on qualifying packages that match spare network capacity without changing contract rates. It requires an existing OnTrac pickup, a minimum weekly volume and a rate-shopping integration; it is being piloted this peak, with early access in the first quarter of 2027. OnTrac also named Arjun Sainath, formerly CTO of Cart.com, chief technology officer.
news.plain: Discounts on volume that is flexible on timing, on top of existing contracts. Early access opens in Q1 2027.

news.title: Cass Freight Index: first annual shipment gain in 42 months
news.sum: The August 2026 Cass shipments index was 1.038, up 2.1% year over year, and expenditures were up 18.7%. FreightWaves reported it was the first year-over-year shipment increase after 42 months of declines.
news.plain: Freight volumes and rates are recovering. The index covers freight, not parcel.

news.title: FedEx publishes Service Guide revision
news.sum: FedEx published a Service Guide revision effective Sep 11, 2026.
news.plain: The Service Guide governs FedEx fees and terms. The revision took effect Sep 11.

news.title: Deloitte expects holiday e-commerce sales to grow 7.5% to 8.4%
news.sum: Deloitte forecasts November–January holiday retail sales of $1.70 trillion to $1.71 trillion, up 4% to 4.8%, and e-commerce holiday sales of $316.1 billion to $318.9 billion, up 7.5% to 8.4%.
news.plain: Online sales are expected to grow about twice as fast as total retail this holiday season.

news.title: Analysis: USPS is no longer automatically the cheapest option for lightweight parcels
news.sum: An industry analysis notes USPS changed its pricing four times in 2026 while alternative carriers kept expanding. It concludes the lowest-cost option for lightweight packages now depends on the package profile and total delivered cost rather than base rates.
news.plain: USPS's 2026 increases narrowed its price advantage on lightweight parcels.

news.title: ShipStation survey: 75% of small merchants say shipping costs rose
news.sum: ShipStation surveyed 868 U.S. retailers with fewer than 500 employees in the second quarter. 75% said shipping costs rose over the past 12 months, 67% spend more than 10% of revenue on shipping and fulfillment, and 47% named carrier rate increases and surcharges as their top peak concern.
news.plain: Small merchants report rising shipping costs as a constraint going into peak.

news.title: UPS revises Rate and Service Guides
news.sum: UPS updated its Daily and Retail Rate and Service Guides effective Sep 7, 2026.
news.plain: The revised UPS guides took effect Sep 7.

news.title: Private equity firm acquires three regional couriers
news.sum: Priority Courier Experts, owned by Trident Management, bought Priority Dispatch and Diamond Expedited in the Midwest and Atlanta-based Inpax, which runs in seven Southern markets including Charlotte and Raleigh. Together they handle more than 1 million pieces a year.
news.plain: The combined courier network handles more than 1 million pieces a year across the Midwest and Southeast.

news.title: Descartes buys 3PL warehouse software firm Extensiv for about $120 million
news.sum: Descartes Systems Group acquired Extensiv, a California provider of warehouse management and fulfillment software for 3PLs, for about $120 million in cash. Extensiv's platform covers inventory, order management, billing and carrier connections.
news.plain: Brings more 3PL warehouse and carrier-connection software under one logistics technology vendor.

news.title: UPS moves to a single global operating model, creates pricing chief role
news.sum: With its Amazon cutback and network overhaul finished, UPS moved to a single global operating model on Sep 1 and reshuffled its top team. It is creating a new Chief Global Commercial Strategy Officer over strategy, product management and pricing; that search is still open.
news.plain: Pricing, product management and strategy move under one new executive role. The search for that executive is open.

news.title: Ship.com and ShipBob add AI agents that can rate-shop and manage shipments
news.sum: Ship.com launched SHIP AI and SHIP MCP, which bring more than 35 rating, labeling and tracking functions into AI apps; more than 30% of orders in its first beta week were bought through the assistant. ShipBob's summer release added an AI agent, an MCP server with read-write access to orders and shipments, and autonomous mobile robots starting in Aurora, Illinois.
news.plain: Carrier selection and label buying increasingly happen inside software agents rather than at the shipper's desk.
news.tie: Shippo launched a similar MCP layer in December 2025.

news.title: Analysis: why more retailers are investing in same-day delivery
news.sum: Modern Retail reported Target's same-day delivery grew 25% and drove 8.7% digital comparable-sales growth, with Target Circle 360 revenue up more than 40%. It also covered Walmart's sub-30-minute delivery in 38 markets and Home Depot's Express Delivery, and cited Roadie's growth as helping lower delivery costs.
news.plain: Same-day is a growing share of retail e-commerce fulfillment, much of it moving outside the national parcel networks.

news.title: Narvar survey: 76% of shoppers would take slower delivery for free shipping
news.sum: Narvar surveyed 1,348 U.S. consumers and 100 retail decision-makers. 76% of consumers would accept slower delivery for free shipping, 37% had a late package last year, and 23% were told a package was delivered when it never arrived. 46% avoid retailers that charge for returns.
news.plain: Consumers still rank free shipping and reliable delivery dates ahead of speed.

news.title: Walmart says U.S. fast delivery grew 48% last quarter
news.sum: Walmart said U.S. fast delivery grew 48% in its fiscal second quarter and that it offers delivery in 30 minutes or less in 38 markets. E-commerce is now more than 23% of its U.S. sales mix. Sam's Club e-commerce rose 26% after it launched one-hour delivery in April.
news.plain: Store-based fast delivery is taking a larger share of retail e-commerce, which reduces the share of that volume moving as traditional parcel.
news.tie: Walmart and Wing said in January they would add drone delivery at 150 more stores in 2026.

news.title: Amazon plans Prime Air drone expansion to nearly 500 towns
news.sum: Amazon said Prime Air will start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from sites near Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland and Syracuse, N.Y., reaching almost 500 cities and towns and 30 million people, up from 11 U.S. locations. Fees are $2.99 per delivery for Prime members (waived on $50+ orders) and $4.99 for others.
news.plain: More small, light Amazon orders could bypass ground last-mile delivery in covered suburbs.

news.title: Gap, Kohl's, Barnes & Noble and Carter's join DoorDash marketplace
news.sum: DoorDash added Gap, Kohl's (its first department store), Barnes & Noble and Carter's for on-demand delivery. DoorDash says more than 500,000 products are now eligible for delivery within an hour. It reported tens of millions of sub-30-minute retail and grocery deliveries in Q1 across more than 22,000 ZIP codes.
news.plain: More general-merchandise orders can be filled from local stores by gig couriers instead of shipped as parcels from distribution centers.
news.tie: Gap's Old Navy joined DoorDash in 2025, and Hibbett added about 1,000 stores in January 2026.

news.title: Home Depot rolls out nationwide Express Delivery from 2,000+ stores
news.sum: Home Depot launched Express Delivery nationwide for a flat per-order fee with no membership, using more than 2,000 U.S. stores as fulfillment points. A Sept. 10 update shortened the promise from three hours to two hours or less. Home Depot says more than 65% of in-stock parcel products already arrive same or next day.
news.plain: More home-improvement parcel orders are filled locally from stores rather than through national carrier ground networks.

news.title: Census: Q2 e-commerce sales up 12.2% to $340.2 billion
news.sum: U.S. retail e-commerce sales were $340.2 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 3.8% from the first quarter and 12.2% from a year earlier, and 17.1% of total retail sales (seasonally adjusted).
news.plain: E-commerce demand, the main source of parcel volume, grew at double digits year over year.

news.title: Serve Robotics expands sidewalk delivery to DC and San Jose
news.sum: Serve Robotics launched robot delivery in Washington, D.C., and San Jose with DoorDash, its seventh and eighth U.S. markets, and began Grubhub deliveries in Chicago, Los Angeles and Alexandria. Serve says it has deployed more than 2,000 robots. Separately, Starship Technologies said in June it will wind down U.S. campus service and move more than 1,200 robots to grocery delivery.
news.plain: Autonomous capacity for short urban deliveries is growing on gig platforms and shifting toward grocery.

news.title: Kroger adds prescriptions to Instacart grocery deliveries
news.sum: Kroger customers can now add pharmacy prescriptions to Instacart grocery deliveries, in as little as 30 minutes, with Harris Teeter following in August. Kroger reported adjusted e-commerce sales up 19% and is scaling back its Ocado-powered fulfillment centers.
news.plain: Another large pharmacy chain now delivers prescriptions locally by gig courier rather than mail-order parcel.
news.tie: Amazon Pharmacy plans same-day prescription delivery in about 4,500 U.S. cities by year-end, and Walmart expanded same-day prescriptions to 49 states.

news.title: FedEx, UPS and DHL begin passing tariff refunds to customers
news.sum: After the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs in February, FedEx began issuing $800 million in refunds without requiring applications. UPS, which said it paid $5 billion on clients' behalf, applied for $500 million in a first phase, with refunds one to three months after Treasury reimburses it. DHL filed claims on nearly all eligible shipments where it was importer of record.
news.plain: Shippers and consignees who paid duties through carrier brokerage are receiving credits in phases set by Customs processing.
news.tie: Proposed class actions filed in February sought enforceable refund obligations from FedEx and UPS.

news.title: Analyst: 2028 UPS–Teamsters outcome will reshape the parcel market
news.sum: ShipMatrix's Satish Jindel argues that if UPS takes a hard line and leans on its Roadie gig network it could dominate, while accepting union demands could shrink it. He expects FedEx to gain once Network 2.0 lowers its costs, and regional startups to be squeezed or bought.
news.plain: Analysis, not an announcement. ShipMatrix's Satish Jindel says UPS labor costs run well above contractor and gig networks.

news.title: Postmaster General says Senate ZIP code bill would cost over $800 million
news.sum: The bill would give 83 communities with split ZIP codes their own code. It cleared committee 10–3 and awaits a full Senate vote. Postmaster General David Steiner says it would cost well over $800 million and could force post office consolidations; USPS has lost $14.7 billion in 21 months.
news.plain: No change to postal rates. The bill awaits a full Senate vote.

news.title: UPS adds pickup dashboard and faster label tools for small businesses
news.sum: UPS rolled out an online dashboard to schedule, manage and track pickups with real-time updates, more control over on-demand Smart Pickups, single-screen label creation, and more mobile features.
news.plain: UPS says on-demand Smart Pickups can cost up to 50% less than scheduled daily pickups.

news.title: Salesforce: retailers to spend $3 billion more on free shipping this holiday season
news.sum: Salesforce predicts 20% of 2026 holiday e-commerce traffic will come from AI agents and says free shipping is the top purchase factor at every income level. It expects retailers to spend an additional $3 billion globally on free shipping, a 7% year-over-year cost increase.
news.plain: Retailers' cost of offering free shipping keeps rising through the 2026 peak.

news.title: UPS second-quarter revenue tops estimates at $22.8B
news.sum: UPS reported second-quarter revenue of about $22.83 billion, ahead of estimates near $21.84 billion. Third-quarter results come Oct 27.
news.plain: No rate change. UPS reports higher revenue per piece as lower-yield volume declines.

news.title: Instacart signs non-grocery retailers: Tractor Supply, Foot Locker, Petsense, World Market
news.sum: Instacart added a run of non-grocery retailers this summer: Tractor Supply (2,400+ stores, July 15), Foot Locker, Kids Foot Locker and Champs Sports (1,000+ locations, Aug. 19), Tractor Supply's Petsense (130+ stores, exclusive, Aug. 26) and World Market (248 stores, exclusive, Sept. 2). All offer delivery in as little as an hour with no markup.
news.plain: Heavy and bulky items such as feed, pet food and footwear can now be filled from local stores instead of shipped as weight-priced ground parcels.
news.tie: Gopuff said Sept. 22 it will join the Instacart marketplace using its own micro-fulfillment centers.

news.title: Zipline plans Austin and Cleveland launches, including Cleveland Clinic prescriptions
news.sum: Zipline announced launches in Austin and Cleveland, including its first U.S. home prescription delivery service with Cleveland Clinic. It reports more than 2.5 million commercial deliveries and says merchants on its app grew 13-fold in the first half of 2026.
news.plain: Drone delivery is extending to health-system prescriptions as well as restaurant and retail orders.
news.tie: Zipline raised more than $600 million in January at a $7.6 billion valuation.

news.title: FedEx launches a dedicated life sciences unit
news.sum: FedEx created FedEx Life Sciences for pharma, medical devices, biologics and clinical-trial shipments. FedEx puts its healthcare revenue at about $10 billion and runs six Life Science Centers. Supply Chain Dive later reported 40% of FedEx healthcare customers use its FedEx Surround monitoring service.
news.plain: UPS and FedEx now both run dedicated healthcare units competing for temperature-sensitive parcel and express volume.
news.tie: UPS reported $11.2 billion in 2025 healthcare revenue.

news.title: Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index: 23.1 billion U.S. parcels in 2025, forecast 31 billion by 2031
news.sum: Pitney Bowes put 2025 U.S. parcel volume at 23.1 billion (+3.3%), with revenue up 6.2% and revenue per parcel at $9.34. Amazon Logistics handled 6.9 billion, USPS 6.2 billion, UPS 4.3 billion and FedEx 3.9 billion. By revenue, UPS held 31.6%, FedEx 30.8%, Amazon 15.5% and USPS 14.9%. Its most-likely forecast is about 31 billion parcels by 2031.
news.plain: A second benchmark that also ranks Amazon first by volume; its totals differ from ShipMatrix's, so the two are separate estimates.
news.tie: ShipMatrix's March release put 2025 volume at 23.9 billion.

news.title: UPS invests $48 million in 27 temperature-controlled cross-docks
news.sum: UPS is investing $48 million in 27 temperature-controlled freight cross-docks across the U.S., Europe, Asia and the Americas, described as IATA CEIV Pharma–compliant and monitored around the clock. UPS says more than 85% of newly approved biologics need temperature control.
news.plain: Adds cold-chain handling capacity inside a carrier network for pharma shippers.
news.tie: Follows UPS's $1.6 billion purchase of Andlauer Healthcare, completed in November 2025.

news.title: AlixPartners: 83% of retailers report higher home delivery costs
news.sum: AlixPartners' 14th annual home delivery survey found 64% of executives say home delivery is not yet profitable and 83% of retailers report higher delivery costs than a year ago. Consumers expect free delivery in an average of 2.7 days, down from more than 3.5 days.
news.plain: Delivery costs are rising while consumers expect faster free delivery.

news.title: UPS rolls out AI tools for customer service, customs and returns
news.sum: UPS expects AI and human agents together to handle more than 98% of customer service requests by the end of 2026, with AI assistants in more than 20 countries. UPS says 97% of its shipments clear customs on the first day and its network digital twin updates every 10 minutes.
news.plain: More tracking, claims and customs interactions move to automated channels.
news.tie: FedEx has said it aims to embed AI in more than half of its core workflows by 2028.

news.title: Teamsters vote to challenge UPS over Roadie gig deliveries
news.sum: Teamsters convention delegates unanimously directed leadership to challenge UPS, alleging it routes delivery work to its Roadie gig subsidiary in violation of the 2023 contract. UPS says it complies with the contract and handles disputes through the grievance process.
news.plain: Could limit how UPS uses Roadie's gig network for same-day and oversize deliveries.
news.tie: In February a federal judge declined to halt UPS's driver buyouts, which were later capped at 7,500.

news.title: Omaha Steaks offers Roadie same-day delivery from all 44 stores
news.sum: Omaha Steaks and Roadie, a UPS company, said same-day delivery covers all 44 Omaha Steaks stores. Customers within 30 miles who order by 3 p.m. ET receive eligible orders in about three hours. Roadie says it has more than 500,000 independent drivers and reaches 98% of U.S. households.
news.plain: UPS's gig subsidiary is taking same-day perishable volume from stores, separate from UPS's union ground network.
news.tie: Teamsters delegates voted June 18 to challenge UPS over work going to Roadie.

news.title: Former drivers sue Amazon and a closed Tennessee delivery contractor
news.sum: Four former drivers for Pave It Forward Logistics, an Amazon delivery contractor that shut down at the end of March, sued the company and Amazon under federal wage and plant-closing laws. They allege the WARN notice was filed two days after the closure and seek unpaid wages, damages and class status.
news.plain: Adds to cases testing Amazon's liability for its delivery contractors' employment obligations.

news.title: DHL eCommerce and USPS sign exclusive last-mile deal worth over $10 billion
news.sum: DHL eCommerce and USPS signed a new exclusive multi-year contract for U.S. last-mile parcel delivery, valued at 'well over $10 billion.' DHL eCommerce runs 19 automated sortation hubs and injects volume into USPS's network of more than 170 million delivery points. The term was not disclosed.
news.plain: Locks in USPS as the final-mile carrier for DHL eCommerce's consolidated lightweight volume, one of USPS's largest wholesale channels.
news.tie: Follows the April 2026 Amazon–USPS agreement that keeps about 80% of Amazon's USPS volume.

news.title: Stord raises $250 million at a $3 billion valuation
news.sum: E-commerce fulfillment provider Stord raised a $250 million Series F led by Strike Capital. It serves more than 1,000 merchants from nearly 100 facilities and has made eight acquisitions, including UPS's former Ware2Go and CEVA's Shipwire. The money goes to AI, robotics and network expansion.
news.plain: Adds a well-funded competitor to Amazon MCF and ShipBob for direct-to-consumer fulfillment and parcel volume.

news.title: PRC: USPS package volume fell 6% in fiscal 2025 while package revenue held flat
news.sum: The Postal Regulatory Commission's analysis of USPS's FY 2025 results found competitive (shipping and package) volume fell 6.0% to about 6.5 billion pieces while competitive revenue rose 0.1%. Competitive products contributed $10.3 billion to institutional costs; USPS's total net loss was about $9 billion.
news.plain: USPS is carrying fewer packages at higher average prices.

news.title: NLRB judge approves Amazon DSP settlement without a joint-employer finding
news.sum: An NLRB administrative law judge approved a settlement in the Battle Tested Strategies case giving about 84 drivers and dispatchers two weeks' pay. The settlement explicitly disclaims Amazon's joint-employer status. The Teamsters called it a 'sham settlement' and sought an appeal.
news.plain: Avoids a precedent that could have made Amazon jointly responsible for DSP drivers, leaving its contracted last-mile model in place.

news.title: UniUni to go public through MAK Acquisition at about $1 billion
news.sum: UniUni, a U.S. and Canadian last-mile carrier, agreed to a reverse takeover by MAK Acquisition Corp., valuing it at about US$1.0 billion and targeting a TSX listing with a later Nasdaq cross-listing. UniUni reports more than 1 million parcels a day and expects over $1 billion in 2026 revenue.
news.plain: UniUni says the proceeds fund automated sort centers to raise capacity to up to 3 million packages a day. Closing is expected in the second half of 2026.

news.title: Amazon opens its logistics network to outside businesses
news.sum: Amazon Supply Chain Services bundles freight, warehousing and parcel delivery for outside companies, including orders from other marketplaces. UPS and FedEx shares each fell about 9 to 10% that day.
news.plain: Amazon now sells freight, warehousing and parcel delivery to companies that do not sell on Amazon.
news.tie: GXO's CEO said May 5 that Amazon's move validates outsourcing; GXO Direct is under 6% of GXO revenue.

news.title: UPS completes Amazon volume reduction and network reconfiguration
news.sum: UPS closed 23 buildings in early 2026 and planned about 30,000 job cuts for the year, after 48,000 in 2025, as it cut Amazon volume by more than half.
news.plain: UPS closed 23 buildings in early 2026 and says it is targeting small and mid-size business volume.

news.title: Uber Eats launches courier pickup for retail returns
news.sum: Uber Eats launched courier returns for eligible retail items of $20 or more bought in the app, priced on courier time and distance; Uber's example fee was $8.25. Launch retailers included Best Buy, DICK'S Sporting Goods, Petco and Pacsun. Refunds start when the courier picks up the item.
news.plain: Created a gig-courier alternative to carrier-label returns for app-purchased retail goods.

news.title: FedEx expands AI, RFID and robotics across its network
news.sum: FedEx says it already plans about 100,000 pickup and delivery routes a day with AI, and is expanding RFID sensors and robotics to improve reliability and the flow of data between shippers and its network.
news.plain: FedEx says it plans about 100,000 pickup and delivery routes a day with AI.

news.title: Amazon and USPS sign new delivery agreement
news.sum: After reports that Amazon would cut its USPS volume by two-thirds, the two reached a new agreement that trims it by about 20%.
news.plain: Amazon's USPS volume falls by about 20% under the new terms, less than the two-thirds cut previously reported.

news.title: Veho reports 68-market network and doubled parcel volume
news.sum: Veho said its network grew 50% year over year to 68 markets covering 46% of the U.S. population, and that it tripled new client launches and doubled parcel volume. Named clients include Sephora, HelloFresh, EssilorLuxottica and Macy's.
news.plain: National retailers have a larger crowdsourced last-mile alternative for residential delivery.

news.title: Amazon passes USPS as largest U.S. parcel carrier by volume
news.sum: Amazon handled 6.7 billion parcels last year versus 6.6 billion for USPS. UPS still earns the most parcel revenue, at $58.3 billion.
news.plain: Amazon handled 6.7 billion parcels to USPS's 6.6 billion. UPS remains largest by parcel revenue.

news.title: ShipMatrix: U.S. parcel volume reached 23.9 billion in 2025; Amazon now the largest carrier
news.sum: ShipMatrix put 2025 U.S. domestic parcel volume at 23.9 billion (+0.4%) and revenue at $196 billion (+4.1%), an average of $8.20 per parcel. Amazon Logistics handled 6.7 billion (+9.9%), USPS 6.6 billion (−8.6%), UPS 4.4 billion (−8.6%), FedEx 3.6 billion (+5.2%) and other carriers 2.5 billion (+13.0%). It forecasts 26.8 billion parcels in 2028.
news.plain: Total volume was nearly flat while revenue grew; Amazon's own network and smaller carriers gained share from USPS and UPS.

news.title: UniUni raises $85 million for sorting automation
news.sum: UniUni closed $30 million in equity led by Rockets Capital and a $55 million credit facility from RBC, bringing total funding to $285 million.
news.plain: The funds go to sorting machines and U.S. and Canadian expansion.

news.title: Thoma Bravo combines WWEX Group with Auctane
news.sum: Thoma Bravo bought WWEX Group, parent of Worldwide Express, Unishippers and GlobalTranz, and merged it with Auctane, owner of ShipStation and Stamps.com. The deal was announced Mar 3 and reported complete by Jun 1; terms were not disclosed.
news.plain: The deal puts a large UPS-reselling network and widely used shipping software under one owner.

news.title: Regional carriers expand coverage and services for 2026
news.sum: Veho launched FlexSave and entered Las Vegas and San Diego. Better Trucks is expanding into Georgia, Florida and the Carolinas. Jitsu opened a Reno hub linking its West Coast network. OnTrac integrated with ShipStation. GOFO acquired Cirro E-Commerce.
news.plain: Regional carrier coverage is widening in the Southeast and West.

news.title: ShipBob report: most brands target 2–3 day U.S. delivery
news.sum: ShipBob's 2026 State of Ecommerce Fulfillment report, based on its customer data and a survey of 416 executives, found 69% of brands aim to deliver U.S. orders in 2–3 days, 80% said 2025 tariff changes raised costs and 84% use a third-party fulfillment company for at least some orders.
news.plain: Most merchants target 2–3 day delivery and fulfill from more than one location.

news.title: ShipMatrix: UPS 97.2%, FedEx 95.3%, USPS 94.1% on time in the 2025 peak
news.sum: For Dec. 1–31, 2025, ShipMatrix measured on-time delivery at 97.2% for UPS, 95.3% for FedEx and 94.1% for USPS. It said the industry delivered about 2.3 billion parcels in the period, up 5% from the 2024 peak.
news.plain: All three national carriers delivered more than 94% of parcels on time during last year's peak while volume grew about 5%.

news.title: OnTrac adds marketplace shipping and sub-1-lb rates in ShipStation
news.sum: OnTrac expanded its ShipStation integration with marketplace shipping, custom delivery instructions and pricing for packages under one pound. Shippers can connect existing OnTrac accounts. OnTrac says its seven-day network reaches more than 75% of U.S. shoppers.
news.plain: Small and midsize shippers can rate-shop OnTrac's lightweight service inside a widely used multi-carrier platform.
news.tie: OnTrac named Mike Brown CEO effective Feb. 1, 2026, citing record 2025 volume.

news.title: FedEx Network 2.0 merges Ground and Express pickup and delivery
news.sum: FedEx is merging its historically separate Ground and Express pickup and delivery operations. It expects the U.S. rollout to be complete by the end of 2027.
news.plain: Pickup and delivery move to one FedEx network area by area, with the U.S. rollout due by the end of 2027.

news.title: NRF and Happy Returns projected $849.9 billion in 2025 retail returns
news.sum: NRF and Happy Returns, a UPS company, projected $849.9 billion in total U.S. retail returns for 2025, with 19.3% of online sales returned and an estimated 9% of all returns fraudulent. The 2026 edition is due this month.
news.plain: Return volumes, which drive reverse-parcel flows, remain very large.

news.title: FedEx 2024 rates take effect; UPS increase already in place since Dec. 26
news.sum: FedEx's 2024 general rate increase, averaging 5.9%, took effect Jan. 1, 2024, following UPS's matching 5.9% average increase that started Dec. 26, 2023. Both averages were down from 6.9% a year earlier.
news.plain: List rates for most FedEx and UPS services are higher for 2024. Long-zone, air and oversized shipments can see increases well above the 5.9% average.
news.tie: Both carriers announced 5.9% averages again for 2025 in Sept.–Oct. 2024.

news.title: USPS shipping price increases take effect, Ground Advantage up 5.4%
news.sum: New USPS competitive prices took effect Jan. 21, 2024: USPS Ground Advantage rose 5.4%, Priority Mail 5.7% and Priority Mail Express 5.9%.
news.plain: Postage for USPS ground and Priority parcels costs more starting Jan. 21, 2024.
news.tie: USPS left these products unchanged in its July 2024 price change.

news.title: UPS cuts 12,000 jobs after weak fourth quarter and soft 2024 outlook
news.sum: UPS said Jan. 30, 2024 it would eliminate 12,000 positions to save about $1 billion, after fourth-quarter revenue fell 7.8% to $24.92 billion. It guided to 2024 revenue of $92 billion to $94.5 billion, below analyst expectations, and said it was reviewing options for its Coyote brokerage unit. Shares fell nearly 9%.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: UPS agreed to sell Coyote to RXO in June 2024.

news.title: Shein and Temu demand reshapes air cargo, with about 600,000 U.S. packages a day
news.sum: A Reuters report on Feb. 21, 2024 said Shein and Temu together send almost 600,000 packages to the U.S. each day. Cargo Facts Consulting estimated Shein ships about 5,000 tonnes a day and Temu about 4,000, which helped tighten air cargo capacity out of China.
news.plain: No change to rates or service. Heavy direct-to-consumer volume from China competes with other shippers for air capacity.
news.tie: In Sept. 2024 the White House proposed limiting de minimis eligibility for these imports.

news.title: OnTrac moves most of its network to seven-day delivery
news.sum: OnTrac began Saturday and Sunday residential delivery for about 75% of its network in March 2024, with weekend deliveries running 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. in eligible areas. The carrier served 35 states and Washington, D.C.
news.plain: Shippers using OnTrac get weekend delivery in most of its footprint without a new service level.
news.tie: OnTrac followed with a Midwest expansion in July 2024.

news.title: UPS plans to close about 200 facilities and triple automated buildings by 2028
news.sum: At its March 26, 2024 investor day, UPS said its Network of the Future plan would close or consolidate about 200 U.S. facilities, close 40 sorts in 2024 and raise the number of automated buildings to 400 by the end of 2028, targeting $3 billion in savings.
news.plain: No change to rates or service; shippers may see pickup and routing changes as buildings consolidate.
news.tie: UPS also brought its SurePost last-mile volume in-house at the end of 2024.

news.title: UPS replaces FedEx as the Postal Service's primary air cargo carrier
news.sum: UPS said April 1, 2024 it would become the main air cargo provider for USPS under a contract of at least five and a half years. FedEx said the two sides could not agree on terms to extend its deal, which runs through Sept. 29, 2024. Financial terms were not disclosed.
news.plain: No change to rates or service for shippers; the switch takes effect after Sept. 29, 2024.
news.tie: FedEx later put the lost USPS contract at a $500 million profit headwind for fiscal 2025.

news.title: Pitney Bowes index: Amazon passes UPS as U.S. parcel volume hits 21.7 billion
news.sum: The Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index, released April 17, 2024, counted 21.7 billion U.S. parcels in 2023, up 0.5%, while revenue slipped 0.3% to $197.9 billion. Amazon Logistics grew 15.7% to 5.9 billion parcels, passing UPS (4.6 billion, down 10.3%); USPS led at 6.6 billion.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: USPS proposes 25% Parcel Select increase for July, holds Ground Advantage flat
news.sum: USPS on May 10, 2024 proposed an average 25% increase for Parcel Select effective July 14, 2024. It proposed no increases for USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail or Priority Mail Express.
news.plain: Shippers and consolidators using Parcel Select face sharply higher postage from July 14, 2024; Ground Advantage prices stay the same.

news.title: Postmaster General pauses mail processing consolidation until 2025
news.sum: In a letter dated May 9, 2024, Postmaster General Louis DeJoy agreed to pause further consolidation of mail processing under the Delivering for America plan until at least Jan. 1, 2025. Senators had cited the new Atlanta regional center in Palmetto, Ga., where only 36% of inbound mail was on time at the end of February.
news.plain: No change to rates; network changes that had slowed USPS delivery in some regions are on hold.
news.tie: USPS released an updated Delivering for America 2.0 plan on Sept. 30, 2024.

news.title: FedEx Express, Ground and Services merge into one Federal Express Corp.
news.sum: FedEx's "One FedEx" consolidation took effect June 1, 2024, combining FedEx Express, FedEx Ground and FedEx Services into Federal Express Corp., with FedEx Freight staying separate. The move supports the DRIVE cost program and Network 2.0, which targets $2 billion in savings by fiscal 2027.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: FedEx announced plans to spin off FedEx Freight in Dec. 2024.

news.title: UPS agrees to sell Coyote Logistics to RXO for $1.025 billion
news.sum: RXO said June 23, 2024 it would buy UPS's Coyote Logistics freight brokerage for $1.025 billion in cash. Coyote had about $3.2 billion in 2023 revenue; the deal makes RXO the third-largest brokered transportation provider in North America.
news.plain: No change to parcel rates or service.
news.tie: UPS first signaled a possible Coyote sale in Jan. 2024.

news.title: FedEx hits $1.8 billion DRIVE savings, takes Network 2.0 to Canada
news.sum: FedEx reported fiscal Q4 2024 revenue of $22.1 billion on June 25, 2024 and said DRIVE cut $1.8 billion in structural costs during the year, with $2.2 billion more targeted for fiscal 2025. Network 2.0 launched in Canada, its largest market yet, and FedEx began a review of FedEx Freight's place in the company. It flagged a $500 million headwind from the end of its USPS contract.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: The Freight review led to a Dec. 2024 spin-off announcement.

news.title: UPS U.S. volume grows for first time in nine quarters; revenue outlook trimmed
news.sum: UPS reported second-quarter 2024 revenue of $21.8 billion, down 1.1%, on July 23, 2024. U.S. volume returned to growth for the first time in nine quarters, but U.S. revenue per piece fell 2.6% on product mix, and UPS set full-year revenue at about $93 billion.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: OnTrac expands to Chicago and the Midwest, reaching 70% of U.S. population
news.sum: OnTrac said July 25, 2024 it had added service in Illinois, Wisconsin, Minnesota and Missouri, bringing it to 35 states plus Washington, D.C., and 70% of the U.S. population. A 334,000-square-foot sort center in Romeoville, Ill., handles the region.
news.plain: Shippers in the Chicago, Milwaukee, Minneapolis–St. Paul and St. Louis areas gain a regional alternative to the national carriers.
news.tie: OnTrac began seven-day delivery in March 2024.

news.title: UPS posts 2024 peak surcharges early, adding a second volume-based demand fee
news.sum: UPS released its 2024 peak tables in July. Additional Handling ($7.75–$9.95), Large Package ($84.75–$99) and Over Maximum ($445–$495) peak fees start Sept. 29, and residential, air and SurePost demand surcharges of $0.25–$2 start Oct. 27. Customers above 20,000 weekly packages can also pay $1.50–$8.25. All end Jan. 18, 2025.
news.plain: Bulky and residential packages cost more from Sept. 29 and Oct. 27, with the highest charges Nov. 24–Dec. 28.
news.tie: FedEx announced a similar structure in Aug. 2024.

news.title: Pitney Bowes exits Global Ecommerce as unit files for Chapter 11
news.sum: Pitney Bowes said Aug. 8, 2024 it sold a controlling stake in its U.S. Global Ecommerce business to Hilco, and two of the entities filed for Chapter 11 to wind down. The unit lost about $136 million in 2023; Pitney Bowes expected exit costs of no more than about $150 million.
news.plain: Shippers that used Pitney Bowes ecommerce consolidation and returns services must move that volume elsewhere.

news.title: FedEx sets 2024 peak surcharges, including new demand fees for ground residential
news.sum: FedEx's 2024 peak fees start Sept. 30 for Additional Handling ($7.75–$10), Oversize ($84.50–$100) and unauthorized packages ($450–$500), and Oct. 28 for demand surcharges. New charges include $0.30–$0.55 on Ground and Home Delivery residential packages and $1.45–$8.25 for enterprise customers over 20,000 packages. All end Jan. 19, 2025.
news.plain: Residential and oversized FedEx packages cost more from Sept. 30 and Oct. 28 through Jan. 19, 2025.
news.tie: UPS published a similar two-tier demand structure in July 2024.

news.title: USPS proposes holiday price increase for Oct. 6 through Jan. 19
news.sum: USPS proposed Sept. 5, 2024 a temporary increase for Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail and Ground Advantage from Oct. 6, 2024 to Jan. 19, 2025. Commercial Ground Advantage rises $0.35 to $5.50 in Zones 5–9 depending on weight.
news.plain: USPS commercial parcels cost more during the holiday window, especially to distant zones.

news.title: White House moves to curb de minimis exemption for tariffed Chinese goods
news.sum: On Sept. 13, 2024 the Biden administration proposed removing the duty-free de minimis exemption, which covers shipments of $800 or less, for goods subject to Section 301, 201 or 232 tariffs. The White House said de minimis shipments had grown from about 140 million to over 1 billion a year.
news.plain: No immediate change; if finalized, many low-value imports from China would owe duties and need more entry data.
news.tie: CBP issued the formal proposed rules in Jan. 2025, citing more than 1.36 billion de minimis shipments in 2024.

news.title: FedEx sets 5.9% average increase for Jan. 6, 2025
news.sum: FedEx announced Sept. 16, 2024 a 5.9% average increase on U.S. domestic, export and import package and freight list rates effective Jan. 6, 2025. Residential, delivery area and additional handling fees also rise, and two-day air and long-distance ground see larger increases.
news.plain: Most FedEx list rates rise about 5.9% on Jan. 6, 2025, more for longer zones.
news.tie: FedEx's 2024 increase also averaged 5.9%.

news.title: Amazon speeds up Multi-Channel Fulfillment and expands Buy with Prime
news.sum: Amazon said Sept. 18, 2024 it cut standard Multi-Channel Fulfillment delivery from five to three business days, with seven-day delivery at no extra cost. Buy with Prime added PayPal checkout and mixed Prime and non-Prime carts on Shopify; orders through merchant sites were up more than 45% year over year.
news.plain: Merchants using Amazon MCF get faster standard delivery at the same price.

news.title: FedEx misses estimates and lowers fiscal 2025 outlook
news.sum: FedEx reported fiscal Q1 2025 revenue of $21.6 billion on Sept. 19, 2024, about flat, with adjusted EPS falling to $3.60 from $4.55. It blamed a shift from priority to deferred services and higher costs, and cut its fiscal 2025 EPS range to $17.90–$18.90.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: DHL Express sets 5.9% average increase for U.S. accounts in 2025
news.sum: DHL Express said Sept. 27, 2024 that U.S. account holders would see a 5.9% general average price increase effective Jan. 1, 2025, along with changes to some services and surcharges.
news.plain: International express shipments with DHL cost about 5.9% more from Jan. 1, 2025.
news.tie: The figure matched FedEx's and UPS's 2025 averages.

news.title: UPS takes over USPS domestic air cargo as FedEx contract expires
news.sum: FedEx's air transportation contract with USPS ended Sept. 29, 2024, and UPS's new contract as primary air cargo provider began the next day. FedEx had flagged a $500 million fiscal 2025 profit headwind and planned to cut related air network costs.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: UPS first announced the deal in April 2024.

news.title: UPS sets 5.9% average increase effective Dec. 23
news.sum: UPS said its 2025 rates for ground, air and international services would rise an average 5.9% effective Dec. 23, 2024, two weeks earlier than the prior year's increase. The average matches FedEx.
news.plain: Most UPS list rates rise about 5.9% on Dec. 23, 2024; actual impact varies by weight, zone and service.
news.tie: UPS's 2024 increase also averaged 5.9%, effective Dec. 26, 2023.

news.title: UPS moves Additional Handling to cubic volume and adds 2% card-payment fee
news.sum: With its 2025 rates, UPS said that from Jan. 27, 2025 the Additional Handling charge will use cubic volume instead of length plus girth, and the Large Package Surcharge will be based on length, weight or cubic volume. A 2% surcharge applies to invoices paid by credit card on or after Oct. 26, 2024.
news.plain: Bulky-but-light boxes may newly trigger UPS handling fees in 2025; paying UPS invoices by card costs 2% more from Oct. 26, 2024.

news.title: Amazon launches Haul, a low-price store shipping from China
news.sum: Amazon introduced Haul on Nov. 13, 2024, a mobile-only storefront with items under $20, most under $10, aimed at Temu and Shein shoppers. Products ship from an Amazon warehouse in China and arrive in about one to two weeks, with free delivery on orders over $25.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: The launch came two months after the White House proposed de minimis limits in Sept. 2024.

news.title: USPS posts $9.5 billion fiscal 2024 loss as package volume rises
news.sum: USPS reported a $9.5 billion net loss for fiscal 2024 on Nov. 14, 2024. Shipping and packages revenue rose 2% to $32.26 billion on 7.25 billion pieces, up from 7.06 billion, while transportation expense fell $1.3 billion. USPS issued its Delivering for America 2.0 plan on Sept. 30.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: USPS proposes 3.9% Ground Advantage increase for Jan. 19, 2025
news.sum: USPS proposed new competitive prices on Nov. 15, 2024, effective Jan. 19, 2025: about 3.9% for Ground Advantage, 3.2% for Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express, and 9.2% for Parcel Select.
news.plain: USPS parcel postage rises again on Jan. 19, 2025, with the largest increase for Parcel Select.
news.tie: Parcel Select had already risen about 25% in July 2024.

news.title: Canada Post strike halts deliveries; USPS suspends mail to Canada
news.sum: About 55,000 Canada Post workers went on strike Nov. 15, 2024. On Nov. 29, USPS suspended international mail services to Canada, including Priority Mail International and First-Class Mail International, leaving U.S. shippers to route Canadian orders through private carriers.
news.plain: Postal shipments to Canada are halted; U.S. shippers must switch to courier services, typically at higher cost.
news.tie: Workers were ordered back on Dec. 17, 2024.

news.title: Canada Post resumes service after back-to-work order ends strike
news.sum: Canada Post operations restarted Dec. 17, 2024 after the Canada Industrial Relations Board ordered about 55,000 striking workers back. Contracts were extended to May 22, 2025, and the strike left an estimated ten million packages undelivered.
news.plain: Postal channels to Canada reopen, though backlogs and a possible renewed dispute in 2025 remain.
news.tie: The strike began Nov. 15, 2024.

news.title: FedEx to spin off FedEx Freight as a separate public company
news.sum: FedEx announced Dec. 19, 2024 that it would separate FedEx Freight, the largest U.S. LTL carrier with $9.4 billion in fiscal 2024 revenue, into an independent public company within 18 months through a planned tax-free spin-off.
news.plain: No change to parcel rates or service; commercial agreements are planned to keep services connected.
news.tie: FedEx began reviewing Freight's place in its portfolio in June 2024.

news.title: UPS ends SurePost handoffs to USPS and takes deliveries in-house
news.sum: UPS's SurePost last-mile arrangement with USPS expired at the end of 2024, and UPS began delivering all SurePost volume itself in January 2025. UPS drivers were already delivering half of SurePost packages in Q4 2024, and the move added about 1.5 million stops.
news.plain: SurePost packages move to UPS drivers, and the service covers only the lower 48 states.
news.tie: UPS renamed SurePost as Ground Saver in 2025.

news.title: UPS takes Ground Saver deliveries in-house, ending USPS final-mile handoff
news.sum: At the start of 2025, UPS stopped handing Ground Saver parcels to the Postal Service for final delivery and began delivering them with its own network, after USPS reworked its agreements with companies using its last mile. UPS also raised Ground Saver rates by nearly 10% on average and limited coverage to the contiguous U.S., excluding PO Boxes.
news.plain: Ground Saver shippers lost PO Box, Alaska and Hawaii coverage and faced higher rates for the economy service.
news.tie: UPS and USPS later reached a new Ground Saver agreement, with handoffs resuming in January 2026.

news.title: UPS completes purchase of European cold-chain firms Frigo-Trans and BPL
news.sum: UPS closed its acquisition of Germany-based Frigo-Trans and sister company BPL, which handle temperature-controlled warehousing, transport and customs for pharmaceutical and biotech shippers. The deal adds storage ranging from cryogenic (-196°C) to ambient conditions to UPS Healthcare.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: UPS followed with a deal for Canada's Andlauer Healthcare Group in April 2025.

news.title: UPS to cut Amazon volume by more than 50% by mid-2026
news.sum: UPS said it will reduce the Amazon volume in its network by more than half by the second half of 2026; Amazon, its largest customer, accounted for nearly 12% of revenue. UPS forecast 2025 revenue of about $89 billion, and its shares fell more than 14% on Jan. 30.
news.plain: No change to rates or service yet; UPS signaled a smaller, more profit-focused network that would shed buildings and capacity.
news.tie: UPS announced 20,000 job cuts and 73 building closures tied to the reduction in April 2025.

news.title: USPS halts, then restores, inbound parcels from China and Hong Kong
news.sum: On Feb. 4, USPS said it would stop accepting inbound parcels from China and Hong Kong after new tariffs and the end of de minimis treatment for Chinese goods were announced. A day later it reversed course and said it would work with CBP on a collection process for the new duties.
news.plain: Cross-border parcels from China briefly faced a postal stoppage; no change to domestic rates.
news.tie: De minimis for China and Hong Kong ended for good on May 2, 2025.

news.title: USPS sets new service standards in two phases starting April 1
news.sum: The Postal Service announced service standard changes for First-Class Mail, Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and other products, rolling out April 1 and July 1 under its Delivering for America plan. Mail collected at some post offices may take an extra day due to regional transportation schedules; USPS projects at least $36 billion in savings over 10 years.
news.plain: Some Ground Advantage and Priority Mail shipments, especially from more remote post offices, may take a day longer.

news.title: Postmaster General Louis DeJoy steps down; Doug Tulino named acting
news.sum: Louis DeJoy announced his exit as Postmaster General, and Deputy Postmaster General Doug Tulino took over on an acting basis until the Board of Governors names a successor. The move came as the administration discussed changes to how the Postal Service is governed.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: The Board named former Waste Management CEO David Steiner as the next Postmaster General in May 2025.

news.title: Amazon resumes Prime Air drone deliveries after two-month pause
news.sum: Amazon restarted drone deliveries in College Station, Texas, and Tolleson, Arizona, after pausing them in January to update software for an altitude sensor issue; the FAA approved the fix. Amazon reiterated its goal of 500 million drone deliveries a year by the end of the decade.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: InPost takes over UK carrier Yodel
news.sum: Poland's InPost acquired 95.5% of JLL, Yodel's parent, by converting a £106 million loan into equity. InPost said the combined UK business could handle about 300 million parcels a year, making it the third-largest independent e-commerce carrier in the UK.
news.plain: No change to U.S. rates or service.
news.tie: The UK market consolidated further when DHL eCommerce UK agreed to merge with Evri in May 2025.

news.title: NLRB complaint seeks to force Amazon to bargain with Teamsters in San Francisco
news.sum: NLRB Region 20 issued a complaint alleging Amazon unlawfully refused to bargain with Teamsters at its DCK6 facility in San Francisco and is seeking a bargaining order. Separately, an NLRB regional office in California has found Amazon to be a joint employer of drivers working for a delivery contractor.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: Amazon is contesting the NLRB's constitutionality in federal appeals courts.

news.title: UPS agrees to buy Andlauer Healthcare Group for $1.6 billion
news.sum: UPS agreed to acquire Canadian cold-chain and healthcare logistics provider Andlauer Healthcare Group for CAD $55 per share in cash, about CAD $2.2 billion (US$1.6 billion). The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2025, pending approvals.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: It follows UPS's January 2025 completion of the Frigo-Trans and BPL acquisitions in Europe.

news.title: UPS to cut 20,000 jobs and close 73 buildings as Amazon volume shrinks
news.sum: UPS said it will eliminate about 20,000 positions in 2025 and close 73 leased and owned buildings by the end of June, targeting about $1 billion in savings from reconfiguring its U.S. network. First-quarter revenue fell 0.7% to $21.5 billion.
news.plain: No change to rates; shippers may see pickup and routing changes as facilities close.
news.tie: The cuts follow UPS's January 2025 plan to reduce Amazon volume by more than 50%.

news.title: Amazon to spend $4 billion expanding rural delivery network by 2026
news.sum: Amazon said it will invest $4 billion by the end of 2026 to expand its delivery network in rural areas, growing its rural footprint to more than 200 delivery stations and creating more than 100,000 jobs.
news.plain: No change to rates; Amazon's own network will reach more small-town addresses that today rely on USPS or UPS.

news.title: De minimis exemption ends for goods from China and Hong Kong
news.sum: The $800 duty-free de minimis exemption ended for Chinese and Hong Kong goods on May 2 under an April executive order. Postal shipments face duties of 120% of value or $100 per item, rising to $200 per item on June 1; other low-value shipments must be formally entered by an importer or broker.
news.plain: Importers of low-value goods from China now pay duties and need customs entries, raising landed costs.
news.tie: The exemption was suspended for all countries on Aug. 29, 2025.

news.title: DoorDash agrees to buy Deliveroo for £2.9 billion
news.sum: DoorDash agreed in May to acquire UK delivery app Deliveroo for 180p per share, valuing it at £2.9 billion. The combined group would operate in 40 countries.
news.plain: No change to U.S. parcel rates or service.
news.tie: The takeover was completed on Oct. 2, 2025.

news.title: USPS names David Steiner as next Postmaster General
news.sum: The USPS Board of Governors selected former Waste Management CEO David Steiner as the 76th Postmaster General, with a July 2025 start expected. Steiner, a FedEx board member, said he would leave that board before joining USPS.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: Steiner succeeded acting PMG Doug Tulino, who stepped in after Louis DeJoy left in March 2025; he began his tenure in July 2025.

news.title: USPS sets July 13 shipping price increases, Ground Advantage up 7.1%
news.sum: The Postal Service's governors approved shipping price changes effective July 13: Priority Mail up about 6.3%, Ground Advantage about 7.1% and Parcel Select about 7.6%, with Priority Mail Express unchanged.
news.plain: Most USPS parcel shippers pay roughly 6-8% more from July 13.
news.tie: USPS later filed temporary holiday surcharges for Oct. 5, 2025 to Jan. 18, 2026.

news.title: FedEx to deliver large packages for Amazon under new multi-year deal
news.sum: FedEx confirmed a multi-year agreement to deliver large packages to Amazon's residential customers, its first major Amazon contract since it dropped Ground and Express work with the retailer nearly six years earlier. Amazon said the deal does not replace UPS capacity.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: The deal comes as UPS cuts its Amazon volume by more than 50% by mid-2026.

news.title: DHL eCommerce UK to merge with Evri
news.sum: DHL Group agreed to combine DHL eCommerce UK with Evri, taking a significant minority stake while Apollo funds stay majority owners. The combined business will handle over one billion parcels a year, and DHL's UK network will be rebranded Evri Premium.
news.plain: No change to U.S. rates or service.
news.tie: The deal followed InPost's April 2025 takeover of Yodel.

news.title: FedEx names leaders for FedEx Freight spin-off, on track for June 2026
news.sum: FedEx named John A. Smith as future CEO and R. Brad Martin as chairman of the independent FedEx Freight, effective at separation. The LTL spin-off remains expected by June 2026.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: FedEx submitted a confidential Form 10 in August 2025 and said the stock would trade as FDXF.

news.title: FedEx raises fuel surcharge tables by about 2 points and updates fees
news.sum: FedEx increased its fuel surcharge tables by generally about 200 basis points for Ground, Home Delivery, domestic package and international services; at $3.74 diesel, Ground fuel rises from 18.5% to 20.5%. FedEx also raised its late payment fee to 9.9% from 8% on June 1 and revised delivery area ZIP codes on June 2.
news.plain: Fuel charges on most FedEx parcels rise about 2 percentage points at the same fuel price.

news.title: UniUni raises $70 million Series D
news.sum: Last-mile carrier UniUni raised US$70 million in an all-equity Series D co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Sinovation Ventures to keep extending its North American network.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: Pitney Bowes: U.S. parcel volume hit 22.4 billion in 2024
news.sum: The Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index put 2024 U.S. volume at 22.4 billion parcels (up 3.4%) and revenue at $203.2 billion. USPS held 31% of volume, Amazon 28%, UPS 21% and FedEx 17%; smaller carriers grew about 23%, and Amazon is projected to pass USPS by 2028.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: FedEx sets 2025 peak surcharges starting Sept. 29
news.sum: FedEx announced holiday surcharges running Sept. 29, 2025 to Jan. 18, 2026: additional handling $8.25-$10.90, oversize $90-$108.50, and residential demand $0.40-$0.65 per package. Shippers over 20,000 weekly residential or Ground Economy packages face a residential delivery charge of $1.55-$8.75.
news.plain: Large and residential FedEx shipments cost more during the holiday period.
news.tie: UPS announced its own 2025 peak fees in early September.

news.title: UPS China-U.S. volume falls 34.8% as tariffs bite
news.sum: UPS reported second-quarter revenue down 2.7% to $21.2 billion, with U.S. average daily volume down 7.3%. China-to-U.S. lane volume fell 34.8% in May and June after higher tariffs and the end of de minimis for Chinese goods; Ground Saver volume fell 23.3%.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: FedEx later cited a $1 billion trade headwind in September 2025.

news.title: USPS files holiday surcharges for Oct. 5 through Jan. 18
news.sum: USPS proposed temporary holiday increases on Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select from Oct. 5, 2025 to Jan. 18, 2026, pending PRC review. Commercial examples include $0.30 for light Priority Mail in Zones 1-4 and up to $13.00 for heavy Priority Mail Express.
news.plain: USPS parcel costs rise temporarily during the holidays, most for heavy and long-zone packages.
news.tie: The July 13, 2025 price change preceded the holiday surcharge.

news.title: De minimis ends for all countries; at least 25 postal services suspend U.S. shipments
news.sum: Duty-free de minimis treatment for imports of $800 or less ended for all countries on Aug. 29 under a July 30 executive order. Postal shipments can pay ad valorem duty or, for six months, a flat $80, $160 or $200 per item; the UPU said at least 25 countries halted postal shipments to the U.S.
news.plain: All low-value imports now owe duties and many foreign postal routes into the U.S. are paused.
news.tie: De minimis ended for China and Hong Kong on May 2, 2025.

news.title: UPS sets 2025 peak surcharges, starting Sept. 28
news.sum: UPS's holiday surcharges run to Jan. 17, 2026: additional handling $8.25-$10.80, large package $90.50-$107 and over-maximum $485-$540 from Sept. 28, plus demand surcharges of $0.40-$2.05 from Oct. 26. Customers over 20,000 weekly packages face up to $8.75.
news.plain: Large, oversize and residential UPS shipments cost more through mid-January.
news.tie: FedEx announced its 2025 peak fees in July.

news.title: OnTrac readies Express and lower-cost Ground Essentials services
news.sum: OnTrac opened early access to OnTrac Express, a 2- and 3-day service using ClearJet air lift, and Ground Essentials, a deferred ground option it says can cost up to 30% less with no residential surcharge. Formal launches are planned for early 2026; OnTrac said domestic shipper volume is up over 40%.
news.plain: Shippers have a new deferred-ground option without a residential surcharge.

srcs.src: Supply Chain Dive via Yahoo Finance

news.title: FedEx sets 5.9% average increase for Jan. 5, 2026
news.sum: FedEx will raise U.S. package list rates an average 5.9% on Jan. 5, 2026, with FedEx Freight up 5.9% or 6.9%. Surcharges also rise, including residential delivery to $6.95 from $6.55 and residential delivery area to $6.60 from $6.20.
news.plain: Most FedEx shippers pay higher base rates and surcharges from Jan. 5, 2026.

news.title: UPS adds per-pound surge fees on import and export services
news.sum: UPS announced peak surge fees on international shipments, including $0.23/lb on Europe-to-U.S. express services and $0.47/lb from India from Sept. 28, plus $0.20/lb on most U.S. export express services from Oct. 26, through Jan. 17, 2026. Shipments to or from China are excluded.
news.plain: International express shipments carry extra per-pound fees during the holidays.

news.title: GOFO commits $150 million to Los Angeles and Newark super hubs
news.sum: Last-mile carrier GOFO said it will invest over $150 million in U.S. super hubs in Los Angeles and Newark, opening in October 2025. GOFO says it runs nearly 100 hubs and stations covering 70% of the U.S. population.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.

news.title: FedEx sees $1 billion hit from end of de minimis and trade shifts
news.sum: FedEx reported first-quarter revenue of $22.2 billion and said the trade environment, largely the end of de minimis, will be a $1 billion headwind this fiscal year. It cut China-U.S. capacity, and said the FedEx Freight spin-off remains on track for June 2026.
news.plain: No change to rates or service.
news.tie: UPS reported a 34.8% drop in China-U.S. volume in July 2025.

news.title: Uber agrees to buy catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion
news.sum: Uber agreed on Oct. 6 to acquire Boston-based ezCater in an all-cash deal valued at $2.3 billion, expected to close in the coming months pending regulatory approval. ezCater works with more than 140,000 restaurants and logged over $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the past 12 months; it will be brought onto Uber Eats and offered through Uber for Business.
news.plain: Businesses that order catering through ezCater may see it fold into Uber Eats and Uber for Business once the deal closes.

news.title: Maersk takes over Puma's three U.S. DCs, will open Torrance site to other brands in 2027
news.sum: Maersk now manages Puma's AutoStore-equipped distribution centers in Torrance, California, Phoenix and Whitestown, Indiana, totaling about 2.3 million square feet, under an agreement announced Sept. 24. Starting in 2027 the Torrance site, rated at about 20 million units of throughput a year, will take on other brands as Maersk's first multi-client AutoStore operation in North America.
news.plain: Brands seeking automated fulfillment near Southern California ports could have a shared-capacity option at Torrance from 2027.

news.title: Amazon to let sellers reach eight countries from one inbound shipment
news.sum: Amazon said its Global Warehousing and Distribution service, live in the U.S., will add the UK, Japan, Germany, France, Italy, Spain and Canada by year-end so one manufacturing run shipped to an Amazon facility near the factory can serve all eight markets. Amazon said storage costs run up to 45% lower than AWD in the U.S. and FBA replenishment up to five days faster, and it also extended AWD to the EU, UK and Australia.
news.plain: Amazon sellers can hold one pool of inventory near the factory and move it into a given country's FBA network only when demand appears there.

news.title: Amazon adds $1.9 billion to its delivery partner program for 2027
news.sum: Amazon said it will invest another $1.9 billion in its Delivery Service Partner program in 2027, aimed at lifting delivery associate pay to a national average of nearly $24 an hour. It also outlined safety and AI tools, including more than 20,000 Smart Delivery Glasses expected in use by the end of 2027, and said its eight-year DSP investment totals $21.7 billion.
news.plain: Higher DSP labor spending is a cost Amazon carries in its own delivery network; the announcement does not change shipper rates.

news.title: Nordstrom looks for carriers to add seven-day delivery, tests same-day beauty in Los Angeles
news.sum: Nordstrom executives said at Parcel Forum '26 the retailer is weighing new entrant carriers to offer weekend delivery at scale, adding to its next-business-day and two-business-day options. A Los Angeles same-day pilot for beauty products delivers orders placed by 3 p.m. by 9 p.m., and the company plans to expand it to more markets this fall.
