news.plain: Large retailers are using carrier mix, including newer entrants, to add weekend coverage the national carriers do not fully provide.

news.title: SPAC sends UniUni breach notice; UniUni lines up new private funding
news.sum: MAK Acquisition Corp., the SPAC that agreed in May to take UniUni public, notified the carrier that its deteriorating finances breached merger conditions, giving it 15 business days to resolve the issue. UniUni announced a term sheet for a private round led by an undisclosed existing investor, saying the money would strengthen its finances ahead of peak.
news.plain: Shippers using UniUni for peak may want to watch whether the merger survives and the new funding closes.
news.tie: UniUni agreed in May to go public through MAK Acquisition.

news.title: Drivers at two DHL Express delivery contractors in Dallas join the Teamsters
news.sum: Fifty-five drivers at DeliverOL and Driven-Force Inc., two contractors delivering for DHL Express from the same facility outside Dallas, voted unanimously to join Teamsters Local 745. The union said it wants to extend protections held by DHL Express's directly employed Teamsters, who ratified a four-year contract this spring.
news.plain: The vote is small but extends union organizing to contracted DHL Express delivery routes.

news.title: DoorDash to pay $131.5 million to settle New York City courier pay claims
news.sum: New York City said DoorDash will pay $131.5 million, including more than $115 million to over 260,000 workers and over $16 million in penalties and costs, after a city investigation found unpaid and late pay between April 2022 and June 2026. Workers will receive about 200% of what they were underpaid, and the settlement adds three years of monitoring and data reporting.
news.plain: Courier pay enforcement in New York adds compliance costs for app-based delivery platforms operating there.

news.title: Watchdog: USPS transportation overhaul slowed package service from rural ZIP codes
news.sum: A Sept. 8 USPS inspector general report found on-time rates for Priority Mail and Ground Advantage were lower on average in ZIP codes under the Regional Transportation Optimization program than elsewhere from October 2024 to April 2026. The program, which adds a transit day for parcels from post offices more than 50 miles from regional plants, is expected to reach 72% of contiguous U.S. ZIP codes; USPS generally agreed with the findings.
news.plain: Shippers picking up or inducting at rural post offices may see an extra day in transit, especially on Priority Mail.

news.title: DHL Express launches Heavy Weight Express for U.S. shippers
news.sum: DHL Express introduced Heavy Weight Express for U.S. businesses, handling up to 2,200 pounds per piece and 6,600 pounds per shipment across more than 220 countries and territories. The service uses DHL's own aircraft and hubs, all-in pricing with no add-on handling surcharges, and dedicated heavyweight desks.
news.plain: International shippers of heavy pieces get an express option priced without separate handling surcharges.

news.title: Shein opens 737,000-square-foot automated fulfillment center in Lebanon, Indiana
news.sum: Shein held a grand opening Sept. 10 for an automated fulfillment facility in Lebanon, Indiana, with a goods-to-person system, scheduled to begin operations in September. The site brings Shein's Indiana footprint to more than 2.5 million square feet.
news.plain: More Shein inventory held in the U.S. means more orders ship domestically rather than directly from overseas.

news.title: DoorDash to buy Grubhub's campus dining unit for $300 million and invest $125 million in Wonder
news.sum: DoorDash said it will invest $125 million in Wonder, Grubhub's owner, and buy Grubhub's campus dining business, live at upwards of 450 campuses, for $300 million. The acquisition is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
news.plain: The deal expands DoorDash's reach into campus food delivery; it does not affect parcel shipping directly.

news.title: FedEx launches Global Trade Navigator tools for international shipping
news.sum: FedEx introduced Global Trade Navigator, including a free Trade Planner on fedex.com for HS codes and duty and tax estimates without a login, plus Ship Manager updates, a Duty and Tax app for Shopify and Global Trade APIs. FedEx cited its 2026 Small Business Trade Index, which found 68% of small and medium businesses regularly see customers surprised by duties at delivery.
news.plain: Cross-border shippers can estimate duties and check classifications before creating a FedEx label.

news.title: Amazon-contracted cargo jet overruns Miami runway, killing five
news.sum: A Boeing 767-300 freighter operated for Amazon by 21 Air overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6 after a flight from San Juan, striking vehicles and catching fire. Five people were killed and five injured, and the NTSB sent a go team to investigate.
news.plain: The NTSB investigation covers a freighter flying in Amazon's air network.

news.title: FarEye survey: U.S. last-mile cost per delivery up 12% for a second year
news.sum: FarEye's Eye on the Last Mile America 2026 survey of more than 500 U.S. delivery operators found median cost-per-delivery inflation of 12% in 2026, matching 2025, and 88% said delivery costs are growing as fast as or faster than revenue. Operators with more control over their networks reported 95% on-time performance and 8.3% cost inflation, versus 65.5% and 14.5% for low-control operators.
news.plain: Last-mile cost growth is running at double digits for many operators, which feeds into delivery pricing.

news.title: ShipStation adds LTL freight booking to its parcel shipping platform
news.sum: ShipStation added less-than-truckload rating, booking, tracking and invoice management alongside parcel shipments, using ShipStation Global's carrier network. Merchants with negotiated LTL rates through Worldwide Express or Unishippers can use them in the platform, and new users can open a freight account without an existing carrier relationship.
news.plain: Small merchants that ship both parcels and pallets can manage both in one system.
news.tie: Thoma Bravo combined WWEX Group with Auctane to form ShipStation Global.

news.title: GOFO doubles Dallas hub capacity to 800,000 parcels a day
news.sum: GOFO added about 200,000 square feet to its Dallas-area hub, doubling daily capacity to 800,000 parcels with a sorter handling 45,000 parcels an hour. The carrier said its network has grown to 300 hubs and stations serving more than 12,000 ZIP codes, about 75% of the U.S. population.
news.plain: GOFO is adding sort capacity in Texas ahead of peak.

news.title: Amazon plans 1-million-square-foot first-mile facility in Norwich, Connecticut
news.sum: Amazon confirmed early planning for a 1-million-square-foot facility in Norwich, Connecticut, that would receive goods and send them to middle-mile sortation centers on a 24/7 basis. No opening date has been set; it is one of two early-stage Amazon projects in the state, along with a fulfillment facility in Killingly.
news.plain: Amazon continues to add Northeast capacity; no timeline yet.

news.title: AutoStore signs global supply agreement with Amazon
news.sum: AutoStore said it signed a framework agreement setting terms for Amazon to procure AutoStore storage and retrieval systems on a global basis. The agreement contains no purchasing commitments at this time.
news.plain: The agreement sets terms but commits Amazon to no purchases yet.

news.title: ClearJet raises $25 million to expand parcel network using commercial flight cargo space
news.sum: ClearJet raised a $25 million growth investment led by Edison Partners, bringing total funding past $40 million. The company moves parcels in unused cargo space on commercial flights across 95 U.S. airports, ships more than 30 million packages a year and works with carriers including OnTrac and Veho.
news.plain: Air-based zone skipping through partners like OnTrac and Veho is another option for faster ground-priced delivery.

news.title: Symbotic installing robotic e-commerce fulfillment system in a Walmart store
news.sum: Symbotic CEO Richard Cohen said the company is installing its SymMicro system in the back of an unnamed Walmart store, expected to come to life in about six months to support pickup and delivery orders. Each station supports 550 picks an hour, and a second site is planned shortly after the first.
news.plain: Walmart is adding automation to store-based fulfillment that powers its fast delivery.

news.title: Senate committee advances bill tying USPS executive bonuses to 95% on-time delivery
news.sum: The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee approved the No Bonuses for Bad Service Act, which would bar extra pay for the postmaster general and deputy in any fiscal year USPS misses a 95% on-time rate for market-dominant mail. A House measure from the Alabama delegation, the PERFORM Act, would also bar bonuses after missed service targets, net losses or adverse audits.
news.plain: The bills target USPS executive pay, not prices or service standards.

news.title: USPS posts $2.5 billion fiscal Q3 loss as package revenue rises 7.7%
news.sum: USPS reported a $2.5 billion net loss for April through June, down from $3.1 billion a year earlier, on operating revenue of $19.9 billion, up 6.1%. Shipping and packages revenue rose 7.7% to $8.25 billion while volume fell 3.4% to 1.554 billion pieces, and USPS said it still faces a severe liquidity crisis.
news.plain: Package revenue is growing on price, not volume, at USPS.

news.title: Report: big-and-bulky last-mile market growth slows to 5.1% a year
news.sum: Armstrong & Associates and the National Home Delivery Association forecast the U.S. 3PL market for delivering oversized items to homes will grow 5.1% a year to $12.3 billion through 2027, down from 10.6% over the past eight years. The report ties the slowdown to weak home sales and higher appliance costs, and ranks RXO, Ryder and J.B. Hunt as the largest providers.
news.plain: Slower demand for heavy home goods is easing growth in white-glove delivery.

news.title: FedEx and Amazon expand robotic arms for loading packages
news.sum: FedEx is expanding Dexterity's dual-arm trailer loading robots at its Hagerstown, Maryland, hub and aims to automate loading and unloading across more than 20 U.S. hubs over the next few years. Amazon said on its July 30 earnings call it plans to more than double its fleet of robotic arms, such as Cardinal and Sparrow, in 2026.
news.plain: Both carriers are automating dock and sort work that drives handling costs.

news.title: Amazon Business adds branded trucks for consolidated business deliveries in 13 states
news.sum: Amazon Business introduced dedicated, branded delivery trucks for organizations that need consolidated drop-offs and palletized delivery at loading docks. The service covers 13 states, including Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, New York and Ohio.
news.plain: Business buyers on Amazon Business in those states can receive consolidated dock deliveries.

news.title: Amazon to refund some customers after recovering about $600 million in tariffs
news.sum: Amazon said it received about $600 million in refunds of IEEPA tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court in February and will automatically refund customers in a limited set of cases where it can trace costs it passed on. It said it is not the importer of record for most items sold in its store and will use the remaining funds to benefit shoppers, including through lower prices.
news.plain: Most tariff refunds flow to the importer of record, so sellers who imported their own goods are the ones positioned to recover them.
news.tie: FedEx, UPS and DHL also began passing tariff refunds to customers in August.

news.title: Walmart and Wing launch drone delivery in Orlando
news.sum: Walmart and Wing began drone delivery from Apopka and Clermont Supercenters near Orlando, covering more than 50,000 homes and businesses, with three more stores planned in the coming weeks. Walmart said the partnership will reach nearly 20 U.S. markets and more than 270 drone locations in 2027.
news.plain: Drone delivery of small store items is expanding across Walmart's Sun Belt markets.
news.tie: Walmart and Wing later said they would add Denver and Seattle in 2027.

news.title: Amazon Q2 sales rise 20% to $200.6 billion as faster delivery and robotics expand
news.sum: Amazon's second-quarter net sales rose 20% to $200.6 billion and operating income rose 43% to $27.5 billion. The company said it partially offset higher transportation costs with an FBA fuel and logistics surcharge introduced in April, and that its 30-minute Amazon Now service reached 80 U.S. cities and towns.
news.plain: Amazon is passing part of its fuel and linehaul costs to FBA sellers through the April surcharge.

news.title: UPS, Amazon and FedEx say fuel surcharges are offsetting higher fuel costs
news.sum: UPS said its fuel costs rose 60.4% in Q2 but surcharges passed them to shippers, leaving a minimal profit impact, while Amazon cited the 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge it applies to FBA since April. FedEx said fuel surcharges added 5 percentage points to Federal Express segment revenue growth in the quarter ended May 31.
news.plain: Fuel surcharges, not base rates, are carrying most of this year's fuel cost increase to shippers.

news.title: DHL eCommerce agrees to buy Baltic parcel carrier Venipak
news.sum: DHL Group signed a definitive agreement for DHL eCommerce to acquire Venipak Group's companies in Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, which run about 800 parcel lockers and a pickup point network. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal is subject to regulatory approvals.
news.plain: The deal extends DHL's own last-mile and locker network in the Baltics.

news.title: USPS launches Local XChange locker handoffs for local marketplace sales for $5.51
news.sum: USPS introduced Local XChange, which lets local buyers and sellers swap marketplace purchases through post office smart lockers for $5.51 per package. Buyers get five days to pick up by QR code, after which the item is held at the counter for 10 more days before returning to the seller.
news.plain: Peer-to-peer sellers have a USPS option that avoids in-person meetups.

news.title: FedEx reclassifies 239 ZIP codes into higher delivery area tiers and adds EU inbound fee
news.sum: FedEx reclassified 239 ZIP codes into higher delivery area tiers on July 20, including 63 moved from extended to remote, the highest-cost tier. For those, FreightWaves lists the delivery area charge at $11.20 per commercial and $7.95 per residential package. FedEx also extended its inbound processing fee to shipments into the 27 EU countries from outside the bloc, effective Aug. 3.
news.plain: Shipments to the reclassified ZIP codes cost more in surcharges.

news.title: Woman sentenced in $150 million counterfeit postage scheme against USPS
news.sum: Lijuan Chen was sentenced to two years and six months in prison and ordered to pay more than $158 million in restitution for a scheme that mailed more than 34 million parcels with counterfeit postage labels from 2020 to 2023. The City of Industry shipping business moved parcels for China-based logistics companies and caused more than $150 million in lost revenue for USPS.
news.plain: USPS continues to pursue postage fraud by package consolidators.

news.title: Maersk opens $100 million fulfillment hub in Hopedale, Massachusetts, for one e-commerce client
news.sum: Maersk said it is investing $100 million in a 617,000-square-foot fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, serving a single large e-commerce customer and creating about 1,000 jobs. The site was set to open in late August with peak throughput of up to 330,000 units a day.
news.plain: Adds high-volume fulfillment capacity in the Northeast ahead of peak.

news.title: USPS mailing price increase takes effect; Forever stamp rises to 82 cents

deals.title: UniUni to go public through MAK Acquisition
deals.sum: UniUni, a last-mile carrier in the U.S. and Canada, agreed to go public through a reverse takeover by MAK Acquisition Corp. at a value of about US$1 billion. It plans a Toronto listing first, then a Nasdaq listing.
who: Last-mile carrier for e-commerce based in Richmond, B.C., founded in 2019. Reports more than 1 million parcels a day; Shein and Temu are customers.
deals.why: UniUni says the proceeds will fund automated sort centers to raise capacity to as many as 3 million packages a day. Closing was expected in the second half of 2026; no closing had been announced as of Oct. 9. On Sept. 24, 2026, MAK sent UniUni a notice of material breach, saying UniUni's financial performance had breached operating limits in the agreement, and said it would terminate if the breach is not cured within 15 days.
